Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level answers up front, and I attached the artifacts you requested to this thread (DPA v1.3 signed, subprocessors CSV, data flow diagram). More detail below.

1) DPA and transfers
- Current canonical DPA: Redwood_DPA_v1.3. We execute our DPA and the standard clauses we accept are the EU SCC Module Two + UK Addendum where applicable. We will sign MedStream's reasonable redlines limited to: stricter data minimization, documented subprocessors notice, and breach notification timing. We cannot accept open-ended territorial indemnities or obligations that require us to hold data only in the EEA without SCCs/legal basis.
- For EEA->US transfers we rely on SCCs and supplemental technical/organizational measures (see section 4 of the attached DPA). We are tracking the incoming EU guidance and will adopt additional controls if regulators require.

2) Subprocessors and notification cadence
- Attached list contains our current subprocessors (compute, monitoring, analytics, backups). Short list highlights: GCP (compute/store), FaunaDB (metadata indexing), Sentry (error monitoring), Mailgun (notifications).
- Notification cadence: we notify customers at least 30 days ahead of material subprocessor additions that may affect data residency. For security-critical subprocessors (e.g., new cloud provider), we notify as soon as contracts are signed.

3) Data flow diagram and PII classification
- See "redwood_data_flow_diagram_2025-07.vsdx". High-level: customer prompts + optional PII fields enter via API or private connectors; tokens and model context are processed in memory-first on GPU nodes; select customer artifacts (logs, compressed caches) are stored in customer-isolated buckets. Personal data that customers explicitly mark as PII is treated per our classification.
- PII categories we use: 
  * Identifiable (names, emails, phone numbers)
  * Sensitive Identifiers (SSNs, health identifiers) — flagged for additional handling and encryption-at-rest with HSM-managed keys where requested
  * Derived/Model Outputs — treated as customer data; customers can opt-out of retention for these

4) Access controls & RBAC
- Internal access is role-based and audited. Production access to customer data requires break-glass justification and two-person approval. All requests are time-limited and logged.
- Admins can't query model caches without documented justification; there's a dedicated audit trail for cache reads.

5) Evidence & artifacts
- Attachments: signed DPA, subprocessors CSV, data flow diagram. We also included a short SOC2 checklist excerpt for questions you marked on the intake.

If you want, we can provide a redline of our DPA with the specific bracketed edits you mentioned. Happy to hop on a quick 30-minute call with Legal to walk through the attachments.

Supplier may engage Subprocessors in accordance with this Section. Supplier will provide Customer with written notice at least thirty (30) days prior to engaging any new Subprocessor.
